title: Equivalence of Brooks' theorem and an edge bound for critical graphs
statement: The following two statements are equivalent. (i) (Brooks' theorem) Every finite nonempty connected graph $G$ that is neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle satisfies $\chi(G) \le \Delta(G)$, where $\chi(G)$ denotes the chromatic number and $\Delta(G)$ the maximum degree. (ii) For every integer $k \ge 4$, every finite nonempty $k$-critical graph $G$ that is not complete satisfies $\nu(k-1) + 1 \le 2\varepsilon$, where $\nu$ is the number of vertices and $\varepsilon$ the number of edges of $G$.
hypotheses_covered: Brooks side: finite nonempty vertex set
Brooks side: G not isomorphic to any odd cycle
Brooks side: G not the complete graph
Brooks side conclusion: chromatic number at most maximum degree
Edge-bound side: finite nonempty vertex set
Edge-bound side: G not the complete graph
